thread:
jamal_support: Heads up — AcmeCorp (acct AC-9872) opened a support ticket: most Dedicated requests in us-east are returning 503 or 4xx with 3–6s tail latency. They say traffic is being routed to eu-west sometimes which doubles latency. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/12345 

alex: Can you paste a minimal repro and any errors from the API gateway? 

jamal_support: Repro: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"test"}'
--- response: 
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
{\"error\":\"Allocation failed: allocator_throttle\"} 

mike_ops: Seeing allocator_throttle in the scheduler logs too. Excerpt from scheduler: 
```
2026-02-12T15:07:12Z scheduler INFO allocate_request req=abcd1234 region=us-east status=throttle reason=insufficient_capacity throttled_until=2026-02-12T15:09:00Z
2026-02-12T15:07:15Z allocator ERROR allocation failed id=abcd1234 err=allocator_throttle:no_free_gpu_pool
```

natasha_capacity: Autoscaler alert just fired: us-east dedicated pool utilization=96%, queue_depth spiked. We hit our burst cap and the allocator started refusing new placements instead of rerouting cleanly. deploy-bot: "autoscale-controller: attempted_burst_increase=2/2 (limit reached)" 

deploy-bot: Alert: autoscaler/us-east-dedicated reached limit, routing policy switched to region-preference=eu-west for new allocations (soft-fallback). 

alex: That fallback is working but it's causing customer-visible latency. Can we confirm if noisy-tenant behavior caused uneven utilization? Any single tenant hogging GPUs? 

mike_ops: Running a quick query: top tenants by GPU minutes last 30m -> tenant:X-99 at 52% of pool, tenant:Y-12 at 18%, rest <5%. Looks like tenant:X-99 is a noisy neighbor. I see repeated long-running sessions pinned to specific nodes: 
```
node-032 gpu0 sessions: 5 (owner: X-99)    runtime: 4h
node-032 gpu1 sessions: 4 (owner: X-99)    runtime: 3.5h
```

jamal_support: AcmeCorp says they also saw 401s intermittently earlier in morning, they questioned billing/auth. I checked — their token was fine. Those 401s correlate with a different customer's spike that hit the auth rate limiter and cascaded into error handling paths. 

oncall-ops: TL;DR: combined issues — (1) noisy tenant X-99 causing local fragmentation, (2) autoscaler hit burst cap and switched to soft-fallback (eu-west), (3) allocator returns throttle instead of queueing in some cases. Need mitigation plan now. 

natasha_capacity: Immediate mitigations: 
- Temporarily evict/limit noisy tenant X-99 to 20% of pool (throttle_by_tenant).
- Manually run rebalance across nodes in us-east to defragment pinned sessions.
- Raise burst-cap limit for 15m to allow backfill (requires ops approval).

alex: Steps I'm taking: 
1) Jamal — tell AcmeCorp we have an ops task in progress and we expect reduced 503s within 15–20m. 
2) Mike — please run: `rbctl rebalance --region us-east --max-parallel 6` and watch GPU eviction warnings. 
3) Natasha — can you open a capacity incident (CI-789) and approve +1 burst for 20m? I'll coordinate the risk. 

mike_ops: Running rebalance now. Command output: 
```
STARTING rebalance job id=rv-20260212-01 region=us-east
draining node-032 (2 sessions moved)
moved session s-998 -> node-045
... done
```

(5m later) mike_ops: Rebalance reduced fragmentation, node utilization smoothed from 96% -> 68% for hot nodes. New allocations are succeeding again. I'm seeing a decrease in allocator_throttle logs. 

natasha_capacity: Burst increase approved for 20m. autoscaler logs: `burst_increase applied=+3` — monitoring. 

oncall-ops: Jamal — please pass on this update to AcmeCorp. Also create a postmortem for tenant X-99 and consider enforcing fairshare limits by default for Dedicated pools. 

jamal_support: Messaged AcmeCorp: "We're seeing an internal tenant causing GPU fragmentation which triggered autoscaler fallback to eu-west; we've rebalanced and temporarily limited the noisy tenant. You should see success rate recover in ~10 minutes. We're following up with a full incident report. Apologies for the disruption." :white_check_mark: 

alex: Follow-ups for the incident runbook: 
- Engineering: add allocator behavior test for throttle vs queued placements when burst cap reached. 
- Capacity: review default burst caps and consider dynamic emergency sloshing. 
- Support: correlate any 401/4xx anomalies to auth rate-limiter backpressure. 

at 2026-02-12T15:45:00Z natasha_capacity: Created CI-789 and linked ticket. Adding action item: trial automatic tenant fairshare at 50% cap for next week in canary region. 

mike_ops: Latest: AcmeCorp confirms success rate back to normal, tail latency dropped. No more 503s in last 12m. I'll keep an eye on allocator_throttle metrics for 1h. 

jamal_support: Closing loop with customer and updating ticket. Will add AMB of incident notes to #postmortems once we have writeup. Thanks team. :pray:
